version.changelog:
- Initial release of the documentation-only skill for APIDot GPT Image 2 API workflows.
- Provides guidance for text-to-image, image editing, image-to-image, reference image generation, async task handling, polling, and webhook setup.
- Contains security practices and integration rules for handling APIDot API keys and async job workflows.
- Offers model-specific routing advice and direct links to official APIDot docs, examples, and support.
- No scripts, APIs, or credentials are included—only documentation and best practices.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only APIDot GPT Image 2 helper with no executable code, hidden automation, or credential storage.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to guide APIDot GPT Image 2 API workflows, and the artifact content stays within documentation, routing links, async workflow advice, and API-key handling guidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are user-directed and include explicit limits such as not making live API calls unless the user asks and not inventing API details.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact contains only SKILL.md and no install hooks, scripts, bundled client code, or automation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It declares an optional APIDOT_API_KEY for real API use, which is proportionate and clearly described as a server-side secret.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No skill-level persistence, privilege escalation, background worker, local indexing, credential harvesting, or automatic network behavior is present; task_id persistence guidance is application-level integration advice.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want APIDot GPT Image 2 workflow guidance. If you later make real API calls, keep APIDOT_API_KEY server-side, avoid logging private prompts or image URLs, and verify current APIDot documentation before implementing request fields.
